svg.title: await hands control back, so the loop can run someone else
svg.desc: Four blocking requests drawn as a staircase totalling 200 ms beside four async requests overlapping into about 50 ms. The event loop is drawn as a four-box cycle: run ready callbacks, fire due timers, block in select until I/O is ready, wake the tasks whose futures resolved. A suspended task card notes that its locals are still alive, and a box containing time.sleep and requests.get is crossed out as blocking the loop. Bars show sequential 2.184 s against asyncio gather 0.081 s, and a semaphore ladder from 19 to 4799 requests per second.
svg.text: await hands control back, so the loop can run someone else
BLOCKING: four tables, one at a time
one task: suspended at await, resumes exactly here.
Its locals are still alive - a frame, not a stack.
this blocks the LOOP. Every other task stops.
use asyncio.sleep, an async client, or asyncio.to_thread.
